messages.content: Quantum entanglement is when two particles become connected in such a way that measuring one instantly affects the other, no matter how far apart they are. If you measure one particle's spin as "up," its entangled partner will instantly be "down," even if it's on the other side of the universe. This isn't because they're sending signals to each other—it's more like they share a single quantum state that only "resolves" when you look at it, which Einstein famously called "spooky action at a distance."
